article.title: Belgium: 70,000-strong anti-austerity demonstration rounds up weekend of mobilization
article.author: Ana Vračar
article.content: A weekend of mobilization in Belgium culminated in a national anti-austerity demonstration in Brussels on Monday, November 23, with unions reporting at least 70,000 participants. After a successful youth strike against militarization and conscription on Friday and a peace march on Sunday, trade unions called on everyone to mobilize against the Arizona government’s devastating budgetary plans. Read more: One million students across Europe strike against war and rearmament “People are already struggling to make ends meet,” Peter Mertens , General Secretary of the Workers’ Party of Belgium (PTB-PVDA), wrote on the day. “They refuse to see billions poured into US-made F-35 fighter jets while we’re told there’s no money to invest in education or healthcare.” “And they refuse to accept that billionaires continue to get off the hook. That is why people are angry. And they have every reason to be.” A staged budgetary deadlock? Bart De Wever’s coalition is aiming to cut at least €10 billion from social security, including healthcare and pension rights, while planning to spend approximately €34 billion on rearmament by 2034. A massive mobilization wave broke out against these plans at the beginning of the government’s tenure and hasn’t stopped since. The pressure has succeeded in winning concessions. More recently, federal budget negotiations have also hit what seems a more substantial obstacle, as coalition partners continue to fail to reach an agreement. Weeks ago, Prime Minister De Wever even offered his resignation to the king – but was rejected . Progressive groups emphasized that De Wever had previously used a similar maneuver to pressure coalition members. And while there is no budgetary agreement yet, PTB-PVDA warns that things would not substantially change even if the social-democratic party Vooruit were to secure the concessions it is seeking. Throughout the weekend, protesters demanded and end to rising military expenses and more investments into social protection. Source: PTB-PVDA/Facebook “The governing parties already agree on most of the austerity package,” PTB-PVDA President Raoul Hedebouw commented last week. “Billions in cuts to healthcare, another attack on wage indexation, higher VAT.” “The real wrangling is over a few hundred million more or less for the so-called broadest shoulders,” he added. “Vooruit needs a symbolic gesture to sell this antisocial agreement. But De Wever refuses even that. The super-rich must be spared at all costs.” “The problem is not the share of the rich in a €10 billion austerity package, but the austerity package itself. Social alternatives to our budget exist. A genuine millionaire’s tax on net assets above €5 million would raise €8 billion a year. We can also phase out the billions in inefficient corporate subsidies and scale back the explosion in military spending.” Protests to break one of the EU’s great taboos The call to reject military investments at the expense of social justice spread throughout rallies over the weekend. On Saturday, approximately 5,000 people protested “to break one of the great taboos of the government and the European Union: spending billions on weapons and preparations for war at the expense of our future,” wrote PTB-PVDA’s Marc Botenga . Approximately 5,000 people marched against war and militarization on Sunday, November 22. Source: PTB-PVDA/Facebook “No,” echoed student organization Comac . “We refuse your billions for war and your cuts to education. We choose peace.”
